description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish staple, a comforting red lentil soup known for its rich flavor and velvety texture. This traditional recipe combines simple ingredients like red lentils, tomatoes, and aromatic spices to create a nourishing and deeply satisfying dish, perfect for any time of year. It is a cornerstone of Turkish home cooking, offering warmth and sustenance in every spoonful.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear; drain well. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic. Have all your ingredients ready for a smooth cooking process.

instructions.title: Saute Onion and Garlic
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Add Tomato Paste and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor. Add 1 teaspoon of dried mint, salt, and black pepper to the pot, stirring to combine with the onion mixture.

instructions.title: Combine with Lentils and Broth
instructions.text: Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot, stirring to coat them with the aromatic mixture. Pour in the hot vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup
instructions.text: Once the lentils are tender, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup until it is smooth and creamy. Alternatively, you can transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender, being cautious with hot liquids. Return to the pot if using a regular blender.

instructions.title: Prepare the Butter Topping
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat until it foams. Add the red pepper flakes (pul biber) and the remaining 1 teaspoon of dried mint. Cook for about 30 seconds, stirring gently, until fragrant. Be careful not to burn the spices.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual serving bowls. Drizzle each bowl with a spoonful of the spiced butter topping. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing, as the lemon brightens the soup's flavors beautifully.

tips: For an extra layer of flavor, you can add a small diced carrot or potato along with the onion in step 2. This will add a subtle sweetness and body to the soup.

The quality of your dried mint and red pepper flakes (pul biber) significantly impacts the final taste. Use fresh, aromatic spices for the best results. You can often find high-quality Turkish spices at specialty food stores.
Mercimek Corbasi thickens as it cools. If you have leftovers, you might need to add a splash of hot water or broth when reheating to achieve your desired consistency.
article:
Discover the heartwarming embrace of Mercimek Corbasi, the beloved Turkish Red Lentil Soup that stands as a cornerstone of Turkish cuisine. More than just a soup, it’s a bowl of comfort, tradition, and vibrant flavor that has nourished generations. From bustling Istanbul eateries to serene village homes, this creamy, nutritious soup is a staple, cherished for its simplicity, affordability, and incredibly satisfying taste. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a curious home cook, diving into the world of Mercimek Corbasi promises a culinary journey filled with aromatic spices and wholesome ingredients.

## What is Turkish Red Lentil Soup (Mercimek Corbasi)?

Mercimek Corbasi, pronounced "mer-jee-MEK chor-ba-SUH," translates directly to "lentil soup." While there are various lentil soups in Turkey, when most Turks refer to "mercimek corbasi," they are almost always talking about this glorious red lentil version. It's characterized by its beautiful reddish-orange hue, smooth and creamy texture (achieved through blending), and a unique flavor profile that is both savory and subtly tangy.

The essence of this soup lies in its humble ingredients: primarily red lentils, which cook down quickly and become incredibly tender. These are typically sautéed with a base of onion, sometimes carrot and potato for added sweetness and body, and then simmered in broth or water. A crucial element that sets this soup apart is the "nane yağı" (mint butter) or "pul biberli yağ" (chili flake butter) drizzle, prepared separately and swirled into each serving, adding a burst of color, aroma, and a final layer of flavor. It’s a soup that embodies the spirit of Turkish hospitality – simple, wholesome, and profoundly satisfying.

## Ingredients for Authentic Mercimek Corbasi

Crafting an authentic Mercimek Corbasi requires a handful of readily available ingredients, each playing a vital role in building its signature flavor and texture.

*   	**Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Use split red lentils, as they cook faster and break down more easily, contributing to the soup's creamy consistency.
*   	**Onion, Carrot, Potato:** These aromatic vegetables form the flavor base. Finely diced, they soften and meld into the soup, adding natural sweetness and depth.
*   	**Tomato Paste (Salça):** A key ingredient that provides umami, a rich color, and a subtle tangy note.
*   	**Butter or Olive Oil:** Used for sautéing the vegetables and creating the flavorful finishing drizzle.
*   	**Chicken or Vegetable Broth:** While water can be used, good quality broth significantly enhances the soup's depth.
*   	**Spices:** Salt and black pepper are essential. Paprika (sweet or hot, depending on preference) adds color and a mild warmth. Dried mint is often incorporated into the finishing butter drizzle, offering a distinctive refreshing aroma.
*   	**Lemon Wedges:** Absolutely indispensable for serving! A squeeze of fresh lemon juice brightens the flavors and balances the richness.

Some recipes might also include a touch of cumin, but the classic Turkish Red Lentil Soup often relies on the simplicity of paprika and mint.

## How to Make Turkish Red Lentil Soup (Step-by-Step)

Making this comforting soup is surprisingly straightforward. Here’s a step-by-step guide to bring the authentic taste of Turkey to your kitchen:

1.  	**Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any impurities and excess starch.
2.  	**Sauté the Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt butter or heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely diced onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
3.  	**Add Vegetables and Tomato Paste:** Stir in the finely diced carrot and potato. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they start to soften. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor and color.
4.  	**Combine Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed lentils to the pot. Pour in the chicken or vegetable broth (or water). Season with salt, black pepper, and paprika. Stir everything together.
5.  	**Simmer:** Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for 20-30 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender and easily mashable. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
6.  	**Blend to Perfection:** Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. Alternatively, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (be cautious with hot liquids), blend, and return to the pot. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot broth or water until you reach your desired consistency. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.
7.  	**Prepare the Finishing Drizzle:** In a small saucepan, melt a knob of butter over low heat. Once melted, remove from heat and stir in a generous pinch of dried mint and a sprinkle of pul biber (Turkish chili flakes) or paprika. This creates the aromatic "nane yağı" or "pul biberli yağ."
8.  	**Serve:** Ladle the hot Turkish Red Lentil Soup into bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the warm mint-butter mixture over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges and crusty bread.

## Tips for the Best Mercimek Corbasi

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Mercimek Corbasi is all about a few key details:

*   	**Rinse Your Lentils:** Don't skip this step! Rinsing removes starch, which can make the soup cloudy and sometimes bitter.
*   	**Sauté Thoroughly:** Allow the onions, carrots, and potatoes to soften and release their flavors fully before adding liquids. This builds a robust base.
*   	**Good Quality Tomato Paste:** Invest in a good quality, concentrated tomato paste for the best depth of flavor and color.
*   	**Blend Until Smooth:** The signature creaminess of Turkish Red Lentil Soup comes from thorough blending. An immersion blender makes this incredibly easy.
*   	**Don't Forget the Lemon:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice at the end is non-negotiable. It brightens the soup, cuts through the richness, and truly elevates the flavor profile.
*   	**The Finishing Drizzle is Key:** The mint-butter or chili-butter drizzle isn't just for garnish; it adds a crucial layer of aroma and flavor that defines the soup.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Turkish Lentil Soup

Mercimek Corbasi is typically enjoyed as a starter or a light meal on its own. Here’s how Turks traditionally enjoy it:

*   	**Lemon Wedges:** As mentioned, a squeeze of fresh lemon juice is essential. Place a wedge on the side of each bowl.
*   	**Crusty Bread or Pita:** Perfect for dipping and soaking up every last bit of that delicious soup.
*   	**Pul Biber (Turkish Chili Flakes):** For those who like a little heat, a sprinkle of dried chili flakes adds a pleasant warmth.
*   	**Pickles (Turşu):** In Turkey, it's common to serve soups with a side of mixed pickles, offering a tangy contrast.
*   	**A Simple Salad:** A light shepherd's salad (çoban salatası) with tomatoes, cucumbers, and onions can complement the soup beautifully.

## Variations & Substitutions for Red Lentil Soup

While the classic Mercimek Corbasi is perfect as is, you can certainly adapt it to your taste or dietary needs:

*   	**Vegan/Vegetarian:** Simply use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth, and opt for olive oil instead of butter for sautéing. The soup is naturally dairy-free if made this way.
*   	**Add More Vegetables:** Feel free to incorporate other finely diced vegetables like celery, bell peppers, or zucchini for added nutrients and flavor.
*   	**Spice It Up:** If you prefer a spicier soup, increase the amount of pul biber in the finishing drizzle or add a pinch of cayenne pepper during cooking. A touch of ground cumin can also be added for an earthy note.
*   	**Herbs:** While dried mint is traditional for the drizzle, fresh parsley or cilantro can be stirred into the soup just before serving for a fresh flavor.
*   	**Thicker or Thinner:** Adjust the consistency by adding more broth/water if you prefer a thinner soup, or simmering a bit longer if you like it thicker.

## Frequently Asked Questions

*   	**Is Turkish Red Lentil Soup spicy?**
    Generally, Mercimek Corbasi is mild. Any spiciness comes from the optional addition of pul biber (Turkish chili flakes) in the finishing drizzle, which can be adjusted to your preference.
*   	**Can I make Mercimek Corbasi ahead of time?**
    Absolutely! This soup often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
*   	**Can I freeze this soup?**
    Yes, Mercimek Corbasi freezes beautifully. Allow it to cool completely, then transfer to freezer-safe containers or bags. It can be frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of water or broth if it’s too thick.
*   	**Is Mercimek Corbasi healthy?**
    Yes, it's incredibly healthy! Red lentils are a fantastic source of plant-based protein, dietary fiber, and essential minerals like iron and folate. It’s a low-fat, nutrient-dense meal.
*   	**What kind of lentils should I use?**
    Always use *split* red lentils for this recipe. They cook quickly and break down easily, giving the soup its characteristic smooth, creamy texture. Whole red lentils will take longer to cook and may not blend as smoothly.

Embrace the warmth and rich tradition of Turkish cuisine by making this incredible Turkish Red Lentil Soup. It’s a simple dish that offers profound comfort and flavor, proving that the most satisfying meals often come from the humblest of ingredients. Enjoy the journey of bringing this authentic taste of Turkey into your home!
